results.name: How to Edit Your Shop’s About Section
results.title: How to Edit Your Shop’s About Section
results.body:
The About section of your shop homepage is where you can share the story of your business. Shoppers can learn more about your creative process, the story behind your products, and any teammates or collaborators you work with.

Share your shop story through a video or photos that show off your workspace or demonstrate your process. You can also add your social media handles, shop members, and more.

How to edit your shop’s About section 

Shoppers can find your About section by scrolling down your shop homepage on the desktop and mobile versions of Etsy.com, or by selecting the About tab at the top of your shop homepage in the Etsy App.

To edit the About section:

  1. On Etsy.com, go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings. 
  3. Select Your shop.

From Your shop, you can edit most of your shop details directly. To customize your shop homepage (including your About section), select Shop home editor in the top right corner.

On Etsy.com, you can also select the pencil icon next to your shop name under Sales Channels to edit this information in the Shop Home editor. Scroll to the About section to edit.

If your shop isn't open to the public, you’ll need to open your shop first.

What can you add to your shop’s About section?

Sharing information about the members and process behind your Etsy shop helps shoppers build a connection and sense of trust with you and your shop.

Shop basics

Make a strong first impression on buyers by sharing your shop’s story and offering a behind-the-scenes look at the creativity and process behind your items.

  • Shop name: Give your shop a unique name. You can change your shop name up to 5 times. After that, additional name changes will require approval from Etsy Support. Capitalization changes or using a previous shop name do not count as a name change.
  • Tagline: Describe your shop in a few words. You can share the story of your shop in more detail in the About your shop section.
  • Logo: Represent your shop with a logo that fits your brand and what you sell. Your logo must be a .jpg, .png, or .gif file, smaller than 10MB, and at least 500px by 500px.
  • About your shop: Share the story behind your business in 5,000 characters or less. You can discuss topics like how your shop was founded, your process, and what you see for your shop’s future. 
  • Featured video: Add a video to your shop home to give shoppers an inside look at your process, materials, workspace, team, or behind the scenes of your shop. Your video must be an MP4, MOV, AVI, MPEG, or M4V file up to 300 MB.
  • Featured photos: Upload up to 5 photos with captions from this section. These can include everything from your creative process to your studio layout. Images can be .jpg, .png, or .gif files up to 2MB. You can upload photos of any dimension you like, but your photos will be cropped to display at 760 x 468 pixels.
  • Links: Share places buyers can get the latest news from your shop, such as a website, blog, or social media profile.

From Shop basics, you can also set preferences for: 

  • Listing sort: Choose which listings are shown first in your shop—either in a custom order you set, or by recency. Buyers can always change their view from a dropdown in your shop home.
  • Sold listings: Select if you want buyers to be able to visit your Sold listings page from your shop home.

Shop team

Let buyers know who helps with making your items or running your shop. People listed here will appear on your shop’s public About page. Owners will also appear on your listing pages.

  • Location: Tell shoppers where you’re based.
  • Shop team: Provide the name, role, and bio of your team members, along with a photo of them. Learn more.

results.name: How to Offer Personalized Listings
results.title: How to Offer Personalized Listings
results.body:
Add Custom options fields to your listings so buyers can personalize the items they purchase. Personalization lets buyers tell you what they’d like customized, like a name for engraving or a special message.
For the buyer, the fields appear on the listing alongside options like color or quantity. You can see the Custom options information a buyer adds on the Orders page.

Jump to a section:

  • How to add Custom options fields to listings
  • What to include in Custom options instructions
  • How to set add-on pricing for Text box fields
  • How to photograph personalized listings
  • When to offer personalizations, variations, or custom listings

How to add Custom options fields to listings

When creating a listing, use Custom options to define the information you want buyers to provide for personalized or customized orders.

You can add up to 5 fields per listing. Each field should focus on a single detail. A simpler setup—using fewer, well-defined fields—can make it easier for buyers to complete their order and provide what you need.

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Listings and select a listing you want to add personalization to.
  3. Under Item options, go to Custom options and select Add field.
  4. Select the field type you want to add and enter the requested information.
    • Select Text box to collect information like names, dates, quotes. 
    • Select List of options to create a list of choices to select from, like fonts and thread colors. 
    • Select File upload to collect images and files from buyers.
  5. Check or uncheck This field is required. 
  6. Choose Done.

  1. Sign in and go to Listings.
  2. Select the listing you want to add personalization to.
  3. Select Custom options, then the field type you want to add and enter the requested information.
    • Select Text box to collect information like names, dates, quotes. 
    • Select List of options to create a list of choices to select from, like fonts and thread colors. 
    • Select File upload to collect images and files from buyers.
  4. Check or uncheck This field is required. 
  5. Choose Done.

To edit a field, select Edit. To delete individual fields, select Delete. 

  1. Go to Listings.
  2. Check the box next to each listing you’d like to edit. 
  3. Go to Editing Options. 
  4. Choose Change Custom options.
  5. Add or edit your fields, then select Apply.

If you enable File upload personalization, content that is submitted by buyers must comply with Etsy’s Buyer Policy. If you’re concerned about a submission, contact Support.

What to include in Custom options instructions

Clear instructions help buyers provide the details you need to complete their order. When creating fields:

  • Use clear titles that describe what buyers should provide.
  • Request one detail per field whenever possible.
  • Explain how or where the personalization will appear on the item.
  • Provide an example when helpful.
  • Include limits, such as character counts or file requirements.

Use this table to decide which field type(s) works best for your listing:

Use a Text box when buyers need to add custom text, like names, dates, or short messages.

Include: 

  • A specific field title that describes what to enter (avoid generic titles like “Personalization”)
  • Instructions explaining how or where the text will appear
  • A character limit (1–1024), based on your design 
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete


Examples of clear, informational Text box fields for a personalized birthday card: 

  1. Title: Name
    Instructions: Enter the name you want to appear on the front of the card [Example: Clifton]
  2. Title: Age
    Instructions: Enter the number you want to appear on the front of the card [Example: 80]
  3. Title: Message for inside (optional)
    Instructions: Enter the text you would like to appear on the inside of the card

Use a List of options when buyers choose from predefined selections like font styles, design variations, or materials. 
You can include up to 30 options. Keeping your list shorter (for example, 10 or fewer options) can make it easier for buyers to choose and complete their purchase. 

Include: 

  • A field title describing the selection
  • One detail per option
  • A logical ordering, if options follow a sequence
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete

Examples of clear, informational List of options fields for a monogrammed sweatshirt: 

  1. Title: Font style (see examples in photo)
    Options: Font 1, Font 2, Font 3, etc. 
  2. Title: Text color
    Options: Black, White, Blue, Red

Use a File upload field when buyers need to upload files, like photos, logos, or artwork.

You can add one upload field per listing. Buyers can upload up to 10 files, with a maximum size of 100 MB per file. Supported file types are .jpg, .png, .svg, .heic, and .pdf.

Include: 

  • A specific field title describing what to upload
  • The number of files
  • Labels, as needed, to identify different files when requesting multiple uploads
  • Instructions explaining what the file should show
  • Whether the field is required or optional for buyers to complete

Use labels when you need buyers to upload different files for specific purposes (for example, “Front of item” and “Back of item”). Labels help clarify what each file should show. If you don’t need different types of files, you can leave labels off and have buyers upload all files together in one place.

The required or optional setting applies to the entire file upload field, not individual labels.

If the field is marked as required, buyers must upload a file for each label before they can check out.

Example of clear, informational File upload field for a locket: 

  1. Title: Pet photos
    Number of files allowed: 2
    Label 1: Left side of locket
    Label 2: Right side of locket
    Instructions: Upload clear, well-lit photos of your pet.

How to set add-on pricing for Text box fields

You can set add-on pricing for optional Text box fields. This lets you charge buyers for text-based customizations, such as embroidery, engraving, or custom messages.

For example, if you offer embroidered names on a sweater, you can create an optional Custom options field and charge an additional $5 when a buyer enters a name.

If you use variations to charge for text-based customizations, consider switching to an optional Custom options field with add-on pricing instead. This lets buyers enter personalization details and see the add-on price in one place.

How to set an add-on price for a Text box field

Add-on pricing is only supported for optional, text-based Custom options fields. Setup and management are available on Etsy.com. Add-on prices are displayed in your shop currency automatically.

  1. Go to Shop Manager and select Listings. Select the listing you want to update.
  2. Under Item options, go to Custom options. 
  3. Select Add field, then Text box, or edit an existing text box.
  4. Mark the field as optional, then enter a price in the Add-on price field.
  5. Publish your changes.

To remove an add-on price, enter $0 in the Add-on price field and publish your changes.

Pricing requirements

Add-on prices must:

  • Be between $0.20 USD and $500 USD equivalent, based on your listing currency
  • Be entered as a numeric value

How buyers see add-on pricing

When a buyer selects a field with add-on pricing, the add-on price is automatically added to the item price. Buyers see the updated total before checkout. The total, including the add-on price, also appears in buyer receipts and order details, as well as seller order details and order management views.

How to photograph personalized listings

Listing images help buyers understand and choose personalization options. Use clear, well-organized visuals to guide buyers through their choices.

Whenever possible, show real, finished items so buyers know what to expect. You may include examples of similar personalized items you’ve previously made, especially to demonstrate options like colors or styles. Be sure to note in your description that these are examples. 

You can include mockups or digital images in additional listing photos to show personalization options. Make sure text is easy to read, with strong contrast and clear fonts. 

For personalized commercial items (such as engraved or monogrammed products), your primary image must show a finished, personalized item similar to the final product. Do not use blank product images or mockups with placeholder text (ex. “Your Text Here”) as the main image. See Listing Image Requirements for more information.

Displaying personalization options in images

When displaying personalization options in images: 

  • Clearly label each personalization option shown in your images
  • Make sure image labels match the options available in your fields 
  • Consider dedicating one image per field so buyers can easily compare choices
  • Ensure text in images has strong contrast and uses an easy-to-read font

When to offer personalizations, variations, or custom listings

Personalization (in Custom options)

  • Buyers enter custom text or information.
  • The input doesn’t impact your product inventory levels.
  • The input contains personalized details for made-to-order items.

Examples of personalization include a name to be engraved, a custom message on a card, and a preferred font or embroidery thread color for a personalized clothing item.

  • Get a buyer’s phone number: If you need a buyer’s phone number for shipping purposes, contact them via Messages.
  • Prompt a buyer to acknowledge they are ordering a digital item: Etsy has taken several steps to address buyer confusion around digital items. Items are marked as Digital Download underneath each digital listing on search results pages, and in the Item details on the listing page. On the Etsy app, buyers see Instant Download on the listing image. 

Variation

  • Buyers choose from a set list of variants of the base item.
  • Each option affects inventory, price or SKU.
  • Stock is tracked for each variation. 

Examples of variations include size, base item color, and material of a clothing item.

Custom listing

You can offer custom listings in your shop by enabling custom order requests. If a buyer requests a custom item, you can convert their request to a custom listing.

  • Buyers submit a request for a one-of-a-kind item based on their specific vision or preferences.
  • The item is for a particular buyer only, so the listing is private and created directly from the original Custom Request Message thread.

Examples of custom listings include a unique sculpture commissioned by a buyer, and a welcome sign for a wedding created to meet a buyer’s specific vision for aesthetic, materials, and more.

results.name: How Etsy's Offsite Ads Work
results.title: How Etsy's Offsite Ads Work
results.body:
Quick Answer

Etsy’s Offsite Ads program promotes your listings across external sites like search engines, social media, and partner networks. You only pay a fee when a buyer clicks an ad and makes a purchase from your shop within 30 days.

In this article:

  • How do Offsite Ads work?
  • How do Offsite Ads fees and enrollment work?
  • When are my orders attributed to Offsite Ads?
  • Where does Etsy advertise?
  • How can I track my Offsite Ads performance?
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Additional resources

How do Offsite Ads work?

You don’t need to take any steps to be eligible for Offsite Ads. Etsy works with partner sites and networks to promote your listings on their pages. Etsy shares listing data (title, images, descriptions, etc.) with ad platforms, and their algorithms match your listing to relevant shoppers.

You can’t choose which listings are advertised. Instead, listings are advertised based on what performs best on each channel. Your listings may be automatically advertised at Etsy’s discretion. To increase the chance of your listings being advertised, improve the quality of your listings. 

How do Offsite Ads fees and enrollment work?

Your Offsite Ads fee rate and enrollment status are based on your shop’s revenue within any consecutive 365-day period:

If you’re a seller with a shop currency other than USD, your revenue total is calculated from your order amounts converted to USD with the currency exchange rates Etsy used at the time that the sale was processed.

How do I opt out of Offsite Ads?

If your shop has never made $10,000 USD or more in any consecutive 365-day period, you can opt out of Offsite Ads. 

  1. On Etsy.com, choose Shop Manager.
  2. Select Settings.
  3. Select Offsite Ads.
  4. Choose Opt out of Offsite Ads.
  5. Confirm that you want Etsy to Opt out of Offsite Ads.

If you want to re-enroll in Offsite Ads, visit the Offsite Ads page and choose Turn on Offsite Ads.

When are my orders attributed to Offsite Ads?

Orders are attributed to Offsite Ads when a buyer clicks on an ad and completes a purchase from your shop within 30 days. If the buyer’s final click before purchasing is through an Etsy Ad instead, only the Etsy Ads fee will apply.

You’re only charged an Offsite Ads fee when a click results in a purchase, there’s no fee if the buyer doesn’t buy anything. A single ad click can lead to multiple attributed orders, so if a buyer makes separate purchases within that 30-day window, each order may incur an Offsite Ads fee.

The Offsite Ads fee for any individual order will never exceed $100 USD, regardless of the order total.

Where does Etsy advertise?

Etsy advertises your listings across search engines, social media platforms, partner sites, and the Google Display Network. These partners may change over time.

Etsy Offsite Ads may appear in the search engines results, platforms, partners and social media sites such as:

  • Google
  • Facebook
  • Instagram
  • Pinterest
  • Bing
  • Etsy Publishing Partner Sites
  • Google Display Network

Learn more and view privacy policies in the Offsite Ad Channels list. 

An Etsy Publishing Partner is a site that offers curated shopping catalogs where Offsite Ads listings may appear. These partners feature curated shopping content where your listings may be promoted.

  • Buzzfeed
  • Martha Stewart
  • Real Simple
  • MyWedding
  • Better Homes and Gardens
  • Lyst
  • Shape

Google Display Network (GDN) lets Etsy advertise to targeted audiences across over 2 million sites. This includes platforms like YouTube, Zillow, Gmail, and Weather.com, reaching users even when they aren’t actively searching. Placements may shift weekly based on user behavior.

How can I track my Offsite Ads performance?

Track stats and performance data, such as revenue, fees, clicks, and ad traffic, through the Offsite Ads dashboard. 

  1. Sign in and go to Shop Manager.
  2. Select Marketing.
  3. Select Offsite Ads.

  • See which search terms and listings drive traffic, then update your titles, tags, and descriptions to better match what buyers are searching for.
  • Identify items that perform well through Offsite Ads and prioritize inventory or production for those items.
  • Look for patterns in clicks and sales so you can plan for seasonal demand or emerging buyer interests.
  • Identify listings that get traffic but not sales and test new photos, pricing, or promotions.
  • See how much of your sales come from Offsite Ads and use that context to guide pricing and margins.

You can also track traffic and visits from Offsite Ads even when they don’t lead to a sale. Since you’re only charged when a purchase is made, this data can help you understand buyer interest and optimize your shop.

Your Offsite Ads fee rate is based on your shop’s revenue within any consecutive 365-day period:

  • If your shop has always made less than $10,000 USD in any consecutive 365 day period, you’ll be charged a 15% fee on the order total for an order attributed to an Offsite Ad.

results.title: What are the Fees and Taxes for Selling on Etsy?
results.body:
When you sell on Etsy, you incur fees for using certain services. 

Your balance from sales, fees, and taxes is calculated and displayed in your Payment account. Learn how to manage your Payment account.

How fees appear in your Payment account

Fees tied to a sale

When you make a sale, certain fees and taxes are tied to that specific sale. They stay in your Pending balance alongside the earnings from that sale. When those earnings clear, the sale’s net amount (earnings minus these fees) moves to your Current balance together. These include:

  • Transaction fees (including shipping and gift wrap transaction fees)
  • Payment processing fees
  • Regulatory operating fees
  • Offsite Ads fees
  • VAT or other applicable seller taxes

Your payment account also shows taxes and government fees paid by the buyer. These are included in the total amount paid by the buyer and then subtracted back out, they are not deducted from your listing price.

Fees charged separately

Other fees and purchases, such as Etsy Ads, shipping labels, listing and renewal fees, and subscriptions like Etsy Plus, are deducted from your Current balance when they’re charged. 

If your Total balance is negative at the end of the month, you’ll have an amount due on the first of the next month. When your outstanding balance is due, you’ll receive an email from Etsy.

To see a breakdown of the fees and taxes associated with a sale, select the order in Recent activities in your Payment account.

Currency conversion

All fixed-cost fees, like listings and Pattern, are published in USD. You can see the fixed USD cost for a fee in its description. Etsy converts fees from USD to your payment account currency at the market rate at the time the fee is reflected in your payment account. This conversion may change if currency exchange rates change.

results.name: How to Add Listing Videos
results.title: How to Add Listing Videos
results.body:
Listing videos give shoppers a better idea of your products, and can also help improve how your listings appear in Etsy search. You can add up to 2 videos per listing.

To add videos to a listing on Etsy.com: 

  1. On Etsy.com, select the Shop Manager icon.
  2. Select Listings.
  3. Choose the listing you’d like to add videos to or create a new listing.
  4. Go to Photo and video.
  5. Drag and drop files or select Upload and choose the short listing videos you would like to add.

To add a video to a listing in the Etsy Seller app:

  1. In the Etsy Seller app, select Listings.
  2. Choose the listing you'd like to add videos to.
  3. Select Listing to see the listing details.
  4. Either select the plus sign under Photo and video or select View all then Add a video.
  5. Choose the short listing videos you would like to add. 

Listing video size and formats

We accept most common video formats for listing videos. The maximum size is 100 MB and file types are:

  • MP4
  • MOV
  • FLV
  • AAC
  • AVI
  • 3GP
  • MPEG

Your video may be 3-15 seconds long and will not contain any audio once uploaded to your listing. While the minimum video resolution is 500px, the ideal video resolution is at least 1080px. You can add two videos per listing. To delete a video, select that video and select the trash can icon.

The video aspect ratio should be 2:1 or 1:2. No matter what kind of device you use to record your video, it’ll most likely already be in a format that is accepted by the video tool. 

Learn more about types of listing videos shoppers love.

results.name: How to Share to Social Media from Your Shop
results.title: How to Share to Social Media from Your Shop
results.body:
Social media is a powerful marketing tool that can help you promote your products, reach potential new customers, and entice existing customers to buy again. 

Tips for using social media as a marketing tool:

  • Post regularly so followers come to expect and look forward to your posts. Create a schedule so you avoid large breaks between posts.
  • Respond to comments to make your customers part of the conversation.
  • Share a mix of posts that promote your products, showcase your process and inspiration, and provide value to your followers.
  • Tailor your posts to each channel to avoid overwhelming your followers with similar content.

How to create a social media post on Etsy

From the Social media section in your shop, you can quickly promote your shop and share important updates to sites like Facebook, Instagram, and X (formerly Twitter).

There are six types of posts you can create through Etsy:

  • Latest listings you’ve added (up to 25 of your most recent listings) 
  • Recent milestones successes, like your shop’s anniversary
  • Current or upcoming sales and coupons 
  • 5-star reviews 
  • Items you’ve favorited 

To create a social media post on Etsy.com:

  1. Go to Shop Manager.
  2. Choose Marketing.
  3. Choose Social Media.
  4. Choose Social accounts to connect an account.
  5. When you’re ready to create a post, select Create post.
  6. Select the type of post you want to create.
  7. Choose Next.
  8. Add images and a caption.
  9. Select the networks you want to share your post with.
  10. Choose Post and continue.
  11. Choose Done

To create a social media post on the Etsy Seller app:

  1. Select More on the navigation bar.
  2. Under Marketing, select Social media.
  3. Select which listing you want to share, which are filtered by Newest, Most favorites, Least views, and Most views.
  4. Select Share listing.
  5. Choose one image or video from your listing to share.
  6. Select Next. 
  7. Select Share. This will save your listing link to your device's clipboard. 
  8. Choose which social media account you want to share your listing on. 
  9. Finish posting your listing. Remember to include the listing link you copied earlier. 

Buyers can buy the items that are tagged in the photos by clicking on the orange price tag or clicking through the listing image on the right of the photo.

To learn more about marketing your Etsy shop, read the Ultimate Guide to Marketing.

results.name: How Does a Buyer Check Out on My Pattern Site?
results.title: How Does a Buyer Check Out on My Pattern Site?
results.body:
Because of enhanced protections for online purchases in the EU, buyers located in those countries may experience issues checking out through Pattern sites. If you have the same listing featured on your Etsy shop, please direct these buyers to complete their purchase there.   

The checkout process on your website is similar to how a buyer purchases on Etsy. When your buyer selects Proceed to Checkout, they’ll be taken to a page where they can choose their payment method. 

If the buyer has an Etsy account, they select the Sign in link. If not, they select a payment method and then select Continue to complete the checkout process as a guest. Guest checkout is not available for:

  • Digital listing purchases
  • Any order over $250
  • Some payment methods, including money orders and checks
  • Orders purchased with Etsy gift cards

If the buyer chooses to check out as a guest, they’ll enter their shipping address, payment details, and email address as they would during usual Etsy checkout. If they signed in to their Etsy account, they’ll see a list of shipping addresses and payment details they saved to their account. They can also add new addresses or payment information.

The Review and submit your order page gives the buyer an opportunity to change their previously entered shipping address, payment method, or email address if needed. They can still use your shop’s coupon codes, even if they are checking out as a guest.

The buyer will get a receipt sent to their email address. They'll also receive a shipment confirmation email (that includes tracking information, if applicable) when you complete the order. If the buyer pays with their PayPal account, these notifications will be sent to their PayPal email address. Otherwise, they'll be sent to the email address they enter during the checkout process. If they signed in to their Etsy account at the time of purchase, we’ll send this information to the email address they have on file.

The buyer will not receive any promotional or marketing emails from Etsy. Also, your buyer won't be sent an email asking them to leave a review, since there is no review system for Pattern sites.

What you'll see

When you get a sale on your site, you’ll fulfill the order the same way as you normally would using your Etsy account. You can find the order on your Open Orders page.

To find the order: 

  1. Go to your Shop Manager.
  2. Select Orders & Shipping.
  3. Choose the Open Orders tab.

If the buyer checked out as a guest, you’ll see the word Guest under their name. You will also see Pattern next to their Order number. 

If a guest buyer registers for an Etsy account and associates their order with their new account, their information will be updated on your Orders page. You’ll now see the buyer’s username and avatar (or if they haven’t chosen their own yet, the gray default avatar). There will also be a link to their Etsy profile. With this in mind, you should always reference order numbers when looking up your orders.

Messages

When a buyer contacts you, either through the Contact us link on your site or their receipt, you'll find their message in your Messages inbox. Your messages to the buyer go to their email inbox. This is where they can reply directly to the message.

Cases

We encourage people who buy from both Etsy shops and Pattern sites to contact their seller directly if they have a question about or an issue with their order.

If a buyer needs to open a case, they’ll need to have an Etsy account. The best way for them to do this is by selecting the order number on their emailed receipt. Learn more about how a buyer reports a problem with a Pattern purchase.

results.name: How to Manage Marketing Settings in Pattern
results.title: How to Manage Marketing Settings in Pattern
results.body:
The Marketing tab of the Pattern Dashboard allows you manage all of your promotional tools for your website. In this section, you can set promotional announcements, create a custom email address, reach new customers through Pinterest and Mailchimp, and track conversion for paid advertising campaigns.

Announcements

This section allows you to create a customized promotional message or shop announcement at the top of your Pattern site. This is separate from the shop announcement in your Etsy shop.

  1. Click Set up an announcement banner.

  2. Write your promotional message or announcement in the text field. There is a 200 character limit.

  3. You also have the option to include a link in your announcement, like a recent blog post or a specific listing you'd like to share. In the Link banner to field, insert your URL and click Done. You can also leave this section blank if you prefer to skip over it.

To make changes to your announcement, click Edit. To remove your announcement completely, click Remove.

Custom email address

This feature allows you to create a professional email address for your brand using the domain name you registered on Pattern. This means you can choose the name displayed before the @ symbol in the email address, like hello@yourdomainname.com.

Note: In order to use Mailchimp from your Pattern site, we strongly recommend having a custom email address. If you don't, your emails to buyers may bounce or go to spam.

Pattern offers custom email addresses that forward to an existing email account that you own. When you receive messages sent to your custom email address, you'll reply and manage these messages from your existing email account.

Messages will arrive in your email inbox folder just like all other emails you receive at this address. We do not create a separate inbox for you to manage, and these emails are not forwarded to the messages feature on Etsy.

If you’d like more control over your professional email address, you can create a custom email by updating the MX record in your DNS settings. You'll see this option in the Domain section of your Pattern Dashboard. This Help article provides steps on how to manage records for your domain.

Custom email availability

This feature is only available to sellers who have registered a domain through Pattern. If you registered for a domain on a third-party site and connected it to Pattern, you’ll need to go through your domain provider to set up a custom email address.

If you have not registered a domain on Pattern and you're using the yourshopname.patternbyetsy.com domain, you will not be able to create a custom email address. You can always set this up in the future if you choose to register for a domain through Pattern.

Setting up

  1. From the Marketing tab of your Pattern dashboard, click Create an @domain.com email alias.

  2. Enter the custom email address you’d like to use. For example: info@yourdomain.com or yourfirstname@yourdomain.com. If you set up email campaigns from Mailchimp, this is the email address people will see in the from line.

  3. Enter the email address that you’d like this email address to forward to. This must be an email account that you own and have access to.

  4. Click Done.

You can edit this address at any time from your Pattern dashboard. If you do change your custom email address, emails sent to the previous custom address will no longer forward to your account. They will also bounce back to the sender as undeliverable.

Note: Emails sent to your custom email address will successfully forward to the preferred email account that you own. However, any emails you reply to will be sent from the original email account instead of your custom email address.

Pinterest verification code

Setting up your Pattern site with Pinterest for Business requires that you confirm your website by inserting a tracking code into your webpage. You can generate this code from your Pinterest settings:

  1. Sign in to your Pinterest account and go to your settings.

  2. Find the Claim section. Enter your Pattern site URL and then click Claim.

  3. Copy the entire tag that displays in the pop-up window.

  4. Go back to your Pattern settings and paste the code into the Pinterest Verification Code field.

  5. Click Publish.

Note: It may take Pinterest up to 48 hours to confirm your website and display your data in their analytics. If you continue to have trouble, please contact Pinterest directly.

Mailchimp integration

This section allows you to connect your site to Mailchimp, an email management service. Once you connect, you can send newsletters to anyone that has opted in to receive these emails.

To learn more about connecting your Pattern site to Mailchimp, check out this Help article.

Conversion tracking

If you have paid advertising campaigns through Facebook or Google, you can track the conversion of these campaigns by adding your conversion tags or codes from the Marketing tab of your Pattern Dashboard.

Google

  1. Sign in to your Google Ads account and copy your conversion tracking Event Snippet code. If you need help creating or accessing your conversion code, follow these instructions from Google. Please note these instructions are for the new Google Ads experience.

  2. Paste the entire Event Snippet code into the Google Conversion Tracking field in the Marketing tab of your Pattern Dashboard. When you're done, click Add.
